# 什么是知识图谱（Knowledge Graph）？

- 原标题：What Is Knowledge Graph?
- 作者：Flavio Amiel Roborank 创始人
- 原文更新日期：2026-07-15
- 原文：https://roborank.io/glossary/knowledge-graph/
- 栏目：[AI Search & GEO](https://roborank.io/ai-search/)
- 说明：中文全文翻译，后附英文原文。原文中的数据、观点、平台说明及推广内容均按原文保留，未经独立验证。

---

## 中文全文

Google 知识图谱是一个结构化数据库，存储现实世界中的实体——人物、地点、组织和事物——以及将它们连接起来的、经过核验的事实与关系。Google 用它将搜索查询理解为概念，而不是一串字符，从而支持知识面板、查询消歧，以及搜索中的各种事实型答案。

### 核心要点

- Google 于 2012 年 5 月 16 日推出知识图谱，由工程高级副总裁 Amit Singhal 宣布，口号是“事物，而非字符串”。
- 发布之初，它包含超过 5 亿个对象以及超过 35 亿条事实与关系，初始数据来自 Freebase、Wikipedia 和 CIA World Factbook 等公开来源。
- 每个实体都有一个稳定的机器标识符，即知识图谱 MID，例如 `/m/0cqt90`。这个标识符独立于人们用来指代事物的任何词语或语言。
- 知识图谱是知识面板、消歧以及生成式 AI 答案越来越依赖的事实依据机制背后的实体层。

### 知识图谱如何运作

一般意义上的知识图谱以网络形式存储信息：现实世界中的每个事物都是一个节点，每项事实则是一条连接两个节点的边。Google 将这种结构应用到整个互联网的规模上。“列奥纳多·达·芬奇”是一个节点，“绘制了”是一条边，“蒙娜丽莎”是另一个节点。存储足够多的这种三元组后，你拥有的就不再是一堆有关某个主题的文档，而是该主题本身的机器可读模型。每个节点都是一个[实体](https://roborank.io/glossary/entity/)，每条边则体现一个由主体、关系和客体组成的[语义三元组](https://roborank.io/glossary/semantic-triple/)。

让这一切真正可用的关键是身份识别。图谱中的每个实体都有唯一的机器标识符——知识图谱 MID，写作 `/m/0cqt90` 这样的形式——它独立于人们所用的名称来标识事物。因此，Google 能把“NYC”“New York City”和“the Big Apple”视为同一个地方，又把“Apple”公司与“apple”这种水果当作不同节点。识别一段文字究竟指向哪个实体，是[命名实体识别](https://roborank.io/glossary/named-entity-recognition/)的工作；图谱则存放识别出来的实体及其相关事实。

Google 根据公开的结构化来源，以及从开放网络中提取的模式构建图谱，再用多个参考来源交叉核实事实，之后才予以采信。实体进入图谱后，会在多个地方发挥作用：帮助消除模糊查询的歧义，为相关搜索旁的[知识面板](https://roborank.io/glossary/knowledge-panel/)提供信息；而且越来越多地为 [AI Overviews](https://roborank.io/glossary/ai-overviews/) 等答案引擎提供事实框架，帮助它们在为响应[建立依据](https://roborank.io/glossary/grounding/)时，让生成的文本始终对应真实、已识别的事物。

### 知识图谱存储什么

图谱由三类相互配合的信息组成：

- **实体**：也就是节点，涵盖具体人物、地点、组织、产品、作品和概念，每个实体都有稳定的机器 ID。
- **事实和关系**：也就是边，包括出生日期、总部所在地等属性，以及“由谁创立”“位于哪里”等关联，以主语—谓语—宾语三元组的形式表达。
- **类型**：为每个实体分配的类别，如人物、地点、组织等，用来限定哪些事实和关系适用于它。

关键区别在于：图谱存储的是*事物及其联系*，而不是网页。一项事实可以被数千份文档交叉证实，一份文档也可以贡献多个实体的相关事实。

### 知识图谱示例

最清楚、且有文档可查的例子，就是知识图谱的发布本身。**2012 年 5 月 16 日**，Google 工程高级副总裁 Amit Singhal 发表了《*Introducing the Knowledge Graph: things, not strings*》，宣布搜索现在能够理解现实世界中的实体及其关系，而不只是匹配关键词字符串。发布时的数字具体且可核验：图谱包含**超过 5 亿个对象**，以及有关这些对象和它们之间关系的**超过 35 亿条事实**。初始数据来自 **Freebase、Wikipedia 和 CIA World Factbook** 等公开来源，之后又以远大于此的规模扩充。

这篇公告将收益归纳为三种具体行为。第一，*找到正确的事物*：搜索“Taj Mahal”时，可以区分泰姬陵古迹、获得格莱美奖的同名音乐家，以及同名赌场，因为它们是图谱中的不同实体，而不只是同一串字符。第二，*获得最佳概览*：Google 可以在一个面板中汇总实体的关键事实。公告提到，当时为 Tom Cruise 展示的信息，已经回答了人们随后关于他的提问中的 **37%**。第三，*探索得更深入、更广泛*：由于实体之间存在联系，图谱可以展示搜索者尚未想到要询问的相关事物。

消歧、概览和关联这三种能力，正是实体模型相对于关键词索引带来的优势，也解释了为什么同一种结构如今支撑着 AI 生成的答案。当助手需要确认“Mercury”指的是水星，而不是汞元素或罗马神祇时，它依靠的仍是 Google 在 2012 年推出的那个理念：先识别事物，再谈论它。

### 人们常犯的错误

人们容易把知识图谱当成某个可以靠优化文案来进入的页面。它不是排名展示位，而是身份层。Google 不会因为你重复某个关键词，就把品牌添加为一个节点；它会这样做，是因为足够多独立、权威的来源，用相同且相互印证的事实描述同一个实体，让系统确信这个事物真实存在，并且具有独立身份。我见过创始人投入大量精力打磨自家网站的措辞，却不理解为什么知识面板始终没有出现；与此同时，真正有效的工作却没有动过：一致的名称、清楚的“关于我们”身份说明，以及在 Google 已经信任的来源上获得佐证。你不是靠写作挤进图谱，而是靠相互印证进入其中。

### 常见问题

#### 什么是 Google 知识图谱？

它是一个结构化数据库，包含现实世界中的实体——人物、地点、组织和事物——以及连接这些实体的事实与关系。Google 用它将查询理解为概念而非文本字符串，从而支持知识面板、消歧以及搜索中的事实型答案。

#### Google 什么时候推出知识图谱？

Google 于 2012 年 5 月 16 日宣布推出知识图谱，工程高级副总裁 Amit Singhal 为此发表了《Introducing the Knowledge Graph: things, not strings》。发布之初，图谱包含超过 5 亿个对象，以及有关这些对象的超过 35 亿条事实。

#### 知识图谱和知识面板是一回事吗？

不是。知识图谱是实体与事实的底层数据库；知识面板只是一个可见的展示界面，呈现其中某个具体实体的部分数据。实体可以存在于图谱中，却从未显示为知识面板。

#### 怎样让我的企业进入知识图谱？

你不能直接把自己添加进去。Google 根据经过交叉印证的公开信息建立实体节点，因此实际可行的路径是：保持名称一致，使用结构化数据，建立权威的身份页面，并在可信的第三方来源上获得引用，而不是只在自己的网站上调整关键词。

### 要点总结

知识图谱是 Google 对现实世界的地图：经过识别的事物通过可核验的事实连接成网，用来把查询理解为一个想法，而不是一种拼写形式。它让搜索从匹配词语转向识别实体，如今又提供了实体层面的基础框架，让传统搜索结果与 AI 生成的答案在需要确定某个名称究竟指什么时，有据可依。

## 英文原文

The Google Knowledge Graph is a structured database of real-world entities — people, places, organizations, and things — together with the verified facts and relationships that connect them. Google uses it to interpret a search query as a concept rather than a string of characters, which powers knowledge panels, query disambiguation, and factual answers across Search.

### Key Takeaways

- Google launched the Knowledge Graph on May 16, 2012, announced by engineering SVP Amit Singhal under the tagline “things, not strings.”
- At launch it held more than 500 million objects and more than 3.5 billion facts and relationships, seeded from public sources including Freebase, Wikipedia, and the CIA World Factbook.
- Every entity gets a stable machine identifier — a Knowledge Graph MID such as `/m/0cqt90` — that names the thing independently of any word or language used to reference it.
- The Knowledge Graph is the entity layer beneath knowledge panels, disambiguation, and the factual grounding that generative AI answers increasingly lean on.

### How the Knowledge Graph Works

A knowledge graph, in the general sense, stores information as a network: each real-world thing is a node, and each fact is an edge that connects two nodes. Google’s Knowledge Graph applies that shape at web scale. “Leonardo da Vinci” is a node; “painted” is an edge; “Mona Lisa” is another node. Store enough of those triples and you no longer have a pile of documents about a topic — you have a machine-readable model of the topic itself. Each node is an [entity](https://roborank.io/glossary/entity/), and each edge is a [semantic triple](https://roborank.io/glossary/semantic-triple/) of subject, relationship, and object.

The step that makes this usable is identity. Every entity in the graph carries a unique machine identifier — a Knowledge Graph MID, written like `/m/0cqt90` — that names the thing independently of the words people use for it. This is what lets Google treat “NYC,” “New York City,” and “the Big Apple” as the same place, and treat “Apple” the company as a different node from “apple” the fruit. Recognizing which entity a piece of text refers to is the job of [named entity recognition](https://roborank.io/glossary/named-entity-recognition/); the graph is where the recognized entities and their facts live.

Google assembles the graph from public structured sources and from patterns extracted across the open web, then corroborates facts across many references before trusting them. Once an entity is in the graph, it surfaces in several places: it disambiguates ambiguous queries, it fills the [knowledge panel](https://roborank.io/glossary/knowledge-panel/) beside relevant searches, and — increasingly — it supplies the factual scaffolding that [AI Overviews](https://roborank.io/glossary/ai-overviews/) and other answer engines use to keep generated text tied to real, identified things when they [ground](https://roborank.io/glossary/grounding/) a response.

### What the Knowledge Graph Stores

The graph is built from three kinds of information working together:

- **Entities** — the nodes: specific people, places, organizations, products, works, and concepts, each with a stable machine ID.
- **Facts and relationships** — the edges: attributes like a birth date or headquarters, and links like “founded by” or “located in,” expressed as subject–predicate–object triples.
- **Types** — a category assigned to each entity (person, place, organization, and so on) that constrains which facts and relationships make sense for it.

The distinction that matters is that the graph stores *things and their connections*, not pages. A single fact can be corroborated by thousands of documents, and a single document can contribute facts about many entities.

### Example of the Knowledge Graph

The clearest documented illustration is the launch itself. On **May 16, 2012**, Google engineering SVP Amit Singhal published *“Introducing the Knowledge Graph: things, not strings,”* announcing that Search now understood real-world entities and their relationships rather than matching keyword strings. The launch numbers are specific and verifiable: the graph contained **more than 500 million objects** and **more than 3.5 billion facts about and relationships between** those objects, seeded from public sources including **Freebase, Wikipedia, and the CIA World Factbook** and then expanded at far larger scale.

The announcement framed the payoff as three concrete behaviors. First, *find the right thing*: a search for “Taj Mahal” could be disambiguated between the monument, the Grammy-winning musician, and the casino, because each is a distinct entity in the graph rather than a shared string. Second, *get the best summary*: Google could assemble the key facts about an entity in one panel — the post noted that the information shown for Tom Cruise already answered **37 percent** of the next questions people asked about him. Third, *go deeper and broader*: because entities are linked, the graph could surface related things a searcher had not thought to ask for.

Those three behaviors — disambiguation, summarization, and connection — are exactly what an entity model buys you over a keyword index, and they are why the same structure now underpins AI-generated answers. When an assistant needs to be sure that “Mercury” means the planet and not the element or the Roman god, it is leaning on the same idea Google shipped in 2012: identify the thing first, then talk about it.

### The thing people get wrong

The thing people get wrong is treating the Knowledge Graph like a page they can optimize copy for. It is not a ranking surface; it is an identity layer. Google does not add your brand as a node because you repeated a keyword — it adds you because enough independent, authoritative sources describe the same entity with the same corroborating facts that the system becomes confident the thing exists and is distinct. I have watched founders pour effort into their own website wording and wonder why no knowledge panel appears, while the actual lever was sitting untouched: consistent naming, a clear "about" identity, and corroboration on sources Google already trusts. You do not write your way into the graph. You get corroborated into it.

### Frequently Asked Questions

#### What is the Google Knowledge Graph?

It is a structured database of real-world entities — people, places, organizations, things — and the facts and relationships that link them. Google uses it to understand queries as concepts instead of text strings, which powers knowledge panels, disambiguation, and factual answers in Search.

#### When did Google launch the Knowledge Graph?

Google announced the Knowledge Graph on May 16, 2012, in a post by engineering SVP Amit Singhal titled “Introducing the Knowledge Graph: things, not strings.” It launched with more than 500 million objects and more than 3.5 billion facts about them.

#### Is the Knowledge Graph the same as a knowledge panel?

No. The Knowledge Graph is the underlying database of entities and facts; a knowledge panel is one visible surface that displays a slice of that data for a specific entity. The graph can hold an entity that never renders a panel.

#### How do I get my business into the Knowledge Graph?

You cannot add yourself directly. Google builds entity nodes from corroborated public information, so the practical path is consistent naming, structured data, an authoritative identity page, and citations on trusted third-party sources — not keyword tweaks on your own site.

### The Bottom Line

The Knowledge Graph is Google’s map of the real world: a web of identified things joined by checkable facts, used to read a query as an idea rather than a spelling. It moved search from matching words to recognizing entities, and it now supplies the entity backbone that both classic results and AI-generated answers reach for when they need to know what a name actually refers to.
